content: Megestrol is prescribed to alleviate symptoms and reduce suffering in patients with advanced breast cancer and advanced endometrial cancer, which originates in the lining of the uterus. The suspension form of megestrol is used to treat appetite loss, malnutrition, and severe weight loss in patients with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). However, it should not be used to prevent appetite loss or weight loss in patients who have not yet developed these conditions. Megestrol is a synthetic version of the human hormone progesterone. It works to treat breast and endometrial cancers by influencing female hormones that contribute to cancer growth. Additionally, it promotes weight gain by stimulating appetite. Megestrol is available as a tablet, a liquid suspension, and a concentrated suspension (Megace ES) for oral administration. Tablets and the regular suspension are typically taken several times a day, while the concentrated suspension is usually taken once daily. It is important to take megestrol at the same time(s) every day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take megestrol exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. Shake the liquid suspension well before each use to ensure even mixing. The concentrated suspension is dosed differently from the regular suspension, so do not switch between the two without consulting your doctor. Do not stop taking megestrol without your doctor’s guidance. Megestrol is sometimes used to treat malnutrition in cancer patients, prostatic hypertrophy (enlargement of the prostate gland), endometriosis (a condition where uterine-like tissue grows outside the uterus), and endometrial hyperplasia (overgrowth of the uterine lining). Discuss the risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. Additionally, ask your doctor or pharmacist for a list of inactive ingredients in the medication. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take. Be sure to mention antibiotics and indinavir (Crixivan), as your doctor may need to adjust dosages or monitor you for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, stroke, diabetes, or kidney or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking megestrol, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication may harm the fetus. Do not breastfeed while taking megestrol. Be aware that megestrol may disrupt the normal menstrual cycle in women. However, this does not guarantee that pregnancy cannot occur. Use a reliable method of birth control to prevent pregnancy. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking megestrol. Unless otherwise instructed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Megestrol may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: impotence, decreased sexual desire, unexpected vaginal bleeding, difficulty falling or staying asleep, gas, or rash. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience nausea, vomiting, dizziness, weakness, blurred vision, extreme thirst, frequent urination, extreme hunger, leg pain, difficulty breathing, sharp or crushing chest pain, chest heaviness, slow or difficult speech, or weakness or numbness in an arm or leg. Megestrol may cause other side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication. Store megestrol in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory, as certain tests may be ordered to monitor your response to megestrol. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
